title: YouTube research with Claude
subtitle: Find what works in your niche, why it works, and what to make next.
hook: Claude can do your YouTube research. Here's the honest setup.
caption:
Claude can do your YouTube research. Here's the honest setup. 👇
The full guide covers it step by step, from collecting transcripts to a monthly routine.

What I'd run:

1/ Gather the material
Copy transcripts from YouTube's Show transcript panel, plus your Studio export.
Claude can only analyse what you give it.

2/ Break down the hooks
Compare the first 30 seconds of the top videos in your niche.
You see which opening moves your niche actually uses.

3/ Find topic gaps
Sort topics into covered well, thin and missing.
Check demand in YouTube's Trends tab before you commit.

4/ Mine the comments
Group public comments into questions and objections.
Objections show which proof to put on screen.

5/ Compare titles and thumbnail text
Describe the wording patterns across a set of videos.
Describe only. Never judge anyone's looks.

6/ Write the outline
Turn the research into a hook and sections.
Leave placeholders for your own examples.

7/ Repeat it monthly
Keep everything in one Claude Project.
Last month's brief stays there to compare against.

Claude doesn't need to watch the videos. This works from text you collect: transcripts, titles, comments and your Studio export. It sorts, compares and spots patterns in that text. That is the slow part of research.

Use other people's videos for private research only. Never republish a transcript.

Setup: one Claude Project, 8 to 12 videos and about 2 to 3 hours for the first run.

Comment YOUTUBE and I'll send you the full guide.

pages.kicker: THE MINI GUIDE · NO FLUFF, JUST STEPS
pages.title: YouTube research with Claude
pages.sub: Find what works in your niche, why it works, and what to make next.

pages.title: Collect text Claude can actually read
pages.body: Give Claude text, not links. Copy transcripts with Show transcript, note titles and views, export your own Studio data, and keep it all in one Claude Project.
pages.prompt: Here is a YouTube link: [link]. Tell me what you can read from it: title, description, transcript, comments, thumbnail. Answer "can read", "cannot read" or "not sure" for each. Do not guess. If you cannot read the transcript, tell me what to paste instead.

ui.title: Research folder
rows: Title table with views and dates

pages.title: Compare how top videos open
pages.body: Paste the first 30 seconds of each transcript. Claude tags the opening move, the promise and the proof offered. You see what your niche does most, and what nobody tries.
pages.prompt: Use the first 30 seconds of each transcript. Make a table: video label, opening move, promise, proof offered, open question. Paraphrase and quote five words at most. List the 3 most common moves. Say if the sample is too small to show a pattern.

pages.title: Spot what is missing in your niche
pages.body: Sort topics into covered well, covered thinly and not covered. Then check demand in the Trends tab in YouTube Studio. A gap can mean nobody wants it, so verify before you film.
pages.prompt: Sort these topics into covered well, covered thinly and not covered. Name the videos behind each claim. Suggest 8 ideas for [audience] and mark each "evidence" or "my guess". Do not invent search volumes. Tell me what to check on YouTube first.

pages.title: Turn comments into video ideas
pages.body: Copy 50 to 150 public comments and remove names and handles. Claude groups them into questions, objections and requests. Objections show you which proof to put on screen.
pages.prompt: Group these comments into themes. For each: label, type (question, objection, request, confusion, praise), rough count using "about", one paraphrase. Flag themes under three comments as weak. List the 5 questions to answer in a video. Do not guess who commenters are.

ui.title: Claude · comment themes
rows: You: Group these comments into themes.
Claude: Which tool to start with (question).

pages.title: Describe the patterns, never the faces
pages.body: List titles with views and dates, and add the words on each thumbnail. Claude describes wording, length and promise types. Describe only. Never ask it to judge anyone's looks.
pages.prompt: Describe patterns in these titles: length, numbers, questions, brackets, promise type. Group by pattern with view counts. Say which comparisons are unfair because of channel size or age. For thumbnails, describe only visible words and layout.

pages.title: Turn research into a script outline
pages.body: Ask for 3 title options, a 20-second hook and 4 to 6 sections, each with proof and what is on screen. Leave placeholders for your own examples. Your experience is what makes the video yours.
pages.prompt: Using this project's research, outline one video on [topic] for [audience]: 3 titles, a 20-second hook, 4 to 6 sections with proof and visuals, and a closing step. Use your own words. Put [YOUR EXAMPLE] where my experience belongs. Ask me first if the research is thin.

ui.title: Outline checklist
rows: Your own example in each section

pages.title: Make it a monthly routine
pages.body: Keep everything in one Claude Project with standing rules. Each month, add new videos and a fresh Studio export, then compare against last month's brief and pick the next two or three ideas.
pages.prompt: You are my YouTube research assistant for [niche]. Use only this project's material and what I paste. Never claim you watched a video. Paraphrase and quote five words at most. Mark each insight "evidence" or "guess". Describe thumbnails neutrally. Ask when my request is unclear.

sources.what: YouTube Help: any video with captions has a transcript you can open with Show transcript in the description.
YouTube Help: YouTube Studio Advanced mode, Export current view, 500-row download limit.
YouTube Help: Trends tab in Studio Analytics, top searches and content gaps.
Claude Help: with web search on, Claude reads pages you link; the article does not mention video or YouTube.
Claude docs: web fetch handles text, HTML and PDF and does not support JavaScript-rendered pages.
